A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAG-3DSG and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 includes Appendix A; v2 ends with references and defers parameter analyses, prompts and runtime profiling to Supplementary Material absent from the supplied PDF. The available content supports comparison, but those deferred materials cannot be assessed.

before.justification: V1 reports original Replica human evaluations, semantic-segmentation and runtime results, component ablations, and an appendix case study.

after.justification: V2 retains original Replica results and reports SceneFun3D/FunGraph3D comparisons, pose-noise experiments, annotator agreement and a physical robot deployment.

M1.justification: The dynamic mapping, re-shot verification, caption clustering, nearest-object RAG and eight-relation pipeline remain. However, v1 Equation 3 explicitly shifts and scales semantic similarity as (cosine + 1)/2, whereas v2 Section 3.1 describes it simply as cosine similarity. The compressed specification does not establish whether the fusion rule changed or its explanation was shortened.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates Replica. V2 retains Replica evaluation and adds SceneFun3D, FunGraph3D, physical indoor robot observations and pose-corrupted reconstruction scenarios. This substantially broadens the represented environments and sensor conditions.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons against Open3DSG, including its fused-node variant, and OpenFunGraph alongside ConceptGraphs and ConceptGraphs-Detector. V1's separate segmentation comparison disappears, removing its comparisons with MaskCLIP, Mask2former plus Global CLIP features, ConceptFusion variants, OpenMask3D and Clio-batch.

E3.justification: V2 introduces evaluation on 20 SceneFun3D and 24 FunGraph3D scenes, object and predicate Recall@K, ground-truth filtering and BERT-based predicate matching. It adds Gaussian pose perturbations with translation standard deviation 0.02 m and rotation standard deviation 1 degree. V1 specifies GPT-4-0613/GPT-4o-mini for its main experiments; v2 evaluates GPT-4o and LLaVA-v1.5-7b variants. The unchanged Replica scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun under the newer configurations.

E4.justification: V2 adds pose-noise stress tests and deployment analysis addressing localization drift, reconstruction ghosting and robustness. The four original component ablations remain, with appendix heatmaps incorporated into Figure 3. V1's detailed LLaVA crop-versus-re-shot case study is absent from the supplied v2.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports an inter-annotator reliability check: three annotators, 100 randomly sampled units and Fleiss' kappa of 0.76, with majority voting for disagreements. V1 provides no corresponding agreement statistic. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or seed-based variability.

E6.justification: V2 adds real-world benchmark and noisy-pose scores in Table 1 and qualitative deployment findings; these concern new settings. V1 Table 1's Replica human-evaluation values remain unchanged in v2 Table 2, while v1's segmentation Table 2 is absent. Overall ablation scores are unchanged, but office0 frequency-weighted IoU is swapped between the full pipeline and w/o Concat: 48.08/30.10 in v1 Figure 5 becomes 30.10/48.08 in v2 Figure 3(f).

T1.justification: V2 retains equivalent voxel-size and view-scoring formulas, including renamed scoring weights. It omits v1's explicit dynamic matching-threshold formula, cluster-score averaging definition and final graph formalization from Sections 3.1.3, 3.2.2 and 3.4. This reduces formal specification; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central noise-reduction and object-level RAG contributions remain. V2 expands the headline claims from improved Replica captioning to state-of-the-art real-world object and relationship prediction, resilience to geometric corruption and readiness for robotic deployment. Its conclusion additionally claims hallucination-free graphs, substantially strengthening the claimed reliability.

C2.justification: V2 attributes relationship gains to reduced propagation of node-caption errors and explains noise tolerance through aggregated geometry, intact crop images and reliable contextual anchors. It discusses ghosting under poor localization and explicitly characterizes the system as offline, proposing future integration as a low-frequency semantic backend. These extend v1's interpretations of component effectiveness and mapping efficiency.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 64 candidate viewpoints, robot sensors and computing hardware, the odometry/data-collection workflow and approximately $0.50 GPT-4o cost per FunGraph3D scene. Conversely, the supplied v2 omits v1's mapping pseudocode, voxel examples, exact CLIP pretraining checkpoint and code/evaluation-script release statement. Further prompts and profiling are deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the dedicated runtime-related-work discussion with viewpoint-aware semantic reasoning. It positions RAG-3DSG against passive frame selection in BBQ, MomaGraph and DAAAM, and connects its active verification framing to Think3D and Chain-of-View. Added functional and dynamic scene-graph literature substantially updates the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around a diagnose-then-rectify and active-photographer framing. Mapping subsections are condensed, experiments are reorganized, and some appendix material moves into the main text. V1's separate ethics, reproducibility and appendix sections are absent from the supplied v2.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redraws Figure 1, introduces a detailed viewpoint-scoring diagram and a robot-deployment figure, and merges v1 Figures 3 and 5 into a six-panel ablation figure. The Replica table gains grouped colored headers, and a new real-world comparison table replaces the separate segmentation display. The document format and figure arrangement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's Replica-only evidence through real-world benchmark comparisons, controlled pose perturbations and physical deployment. The annotator-agreement check also improves support for the retained human evaluation. Reduced mathematical and implementation detail, unavailable supplementary material and hallucination-free wording unsupported by the retained 0.82 node and 0.91 edge precision are drawbacks. Nevertheless, the added evidence materially addresses the earlier version's limited support for real-world applicability and robustness.
